subject: Post-call recap: MedSys model-fit & compression fidelity playbook
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Gupta <rajiv@medsys.ai>, Elaine Park <elaine@medsys.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: MedSys model-fit & compression fidelity playbook

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can kick off a focused eval.

Summary from today's discovery:
- Goal: extract structured clinical insights from physician notes and triage escalation triggers with <200ms p99 on inference for short prompts (~120 tokens).
- Data: customer will share a 50k-sample anonymized set (PHI removed) for model validation and prompt tuning.
- Success metrics: entity F1 on our clinician label set, hallucination rate threshold <1.5% on spot-checks, and stepwise throughput at target latency.

Redwood recommendations (initial):
1) Baseline (quality): Llama3-13B / float16 (uncompressed) — use for gold-quality reference.
2) Cost/latency candidates (pick 2):
   - AWQ 4-bit on Llama3-13B (expected ~2.5-3x token throughput vs FP16, small quality delta on clinical NER)
   - GPTQ 4-bit on Mistral-like 7B variant (higher throughput, probable slight drop on long-context extraction)
3) Experimental path: FP8 inference on Llama3-13B for targeted low-latency routes (requires runtime GPU support; we can prototype).

Planned eval assets attached: medsys_promptset_v1.txt (representative prompts and edge cases) and bench_results_seed1.csv (initial microbenchmarks from our lab for reference). Full benchmark dashboard linked below.

Tradeoff considerations to note now:
- AWQ tends to preserve logits ordering better for entity extraction; recommended for early-stage quality-sensitive POCs.
- GPTQ often gives better raw throughput on 4-bit but can introduce tokenization boundary errors for long, nested lists in notes.
- FP8 may beat both on throughput but requires careful calibration and per-prompt QA.

Proposed next steps:
A) Customer: share the 50k sample + S3 read role by EOD Thu 2027-04-29.
B) Redwood: run three 48-hour eval runs (FP16 baseline, AWQ-4 on 13B, GPTQ-4 on 7B) with the attached prompt set and return measurable F1/hallucination/latency reports. Target deliverable: draft eval report by Friday 2027-05-07.
C) Quick sync: 30-min follow-up the week of 2027-05-03 to review results and decide pilot config.

Open asks for Rajiv/ Elaine: confirmation of data delivery timing and any regulatory constraints (e.g., retention window) we should be aware of.

Thanks,
Grace

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: MedSys model-fit & compression fidelity playbook

Thanks Grace — very clear and helpful. A couple of clarifications from our side: 
1) We can get the 50k sample ready; aim to upload by Thu 29th as requested. We'll include a short column that flags high-confidence labeled entities from our in-house annotators.
2) On regulatory: retention needs to be limited to 90 days for this POC; can Redwood commit to that window and provide a quick note on audit logs for access?

On the proposed candidates, Elaine and I prefer starting with the AWQ 4-bit on the 13B as the priority candidate given our accuracy sensitivity. If Redwood's initial run shows <1% hallucination delta vs FP16, we'd be comfortable moving to a short pilot.

Also: what's the estimated cost delta for AWQ vs FP16 for the 48-hour run? Even a ballpark helps for internal approvals.

— Rajiv

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 08:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: MedSys model-fit & compression fidelity playbook

Quick technical notes to set expectations (following Grace's plan):
- AWQ-4 on Llama3-13B: we expect roughly 2.5x token/sec improvement on T4-equivalent nodes, and 3x on Ada-like hardware. Quality-wise, clinically-relevant NER spans generally remain within ~0.5-1.2% F1 delta vs FP16 depending on prompt phrasing.
- GPTQ-4 on 7B: throughput gains can be >3.5x, but watch out for list/number extraction regressions — we should include numeric-heavy prompts in the prompt set (I added several in the attached promptset).
- FP8 path: beneficial for latency if we can run on supported GPUs; we can schedule a short kernel validation but it adds complexity (driver/kernel versions, potential fallback path).

Cost estimate for the 48-hour run (rough ballpark):
- FP16 baseline: $4.5k (cloud compute + infra)
- AWQ-4 on 13B: $1.6k–$2.0k
- GPTQ-4 on 7B: $1.2k–$1.6k
These are approximate and assume continuous runs with our standard throughput config; we'll provide precise numbers in the formal eval report.

I'll own the eval execution; Grace and I will coordinate on promptset tweaks and rollout.

Ben
Ben Carter
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Appreciate the quick replies — happy to lock timelines. Action items I'm recording here:
1) MedSys (Rajiv/Elaine): upload 50k sample to S3 and share access + any label schema notes by 2027-04-29 (noted you are aiming for this). Reply to this thread when done so we can kick runs.
2) Redwood (Ben/Grace/Marissa): finalize promptset (we already dropped numeric prompts and edge-case chains), schedule eval runs to start 2027-04-30 10:00 PT; target completion by 2027-05-02 10:00 PT.
3) Deliverables: bench_results_seed1.csv (internal reference) -> full eval report (PDF + dashboard link) by 2027-05-07. The report will include per-prompt failure examples for any prompt that drops >1.5% F1.
4) Compliance: Grace will send a short retention/audit note confirming 90-day retention and access logs.

If Rajiv confirmed the upload today we can go ahead and spin up the first runs this afternoon. Otherwise we will wait until S3 access is visible.

Thanks — I'll schedule the 30-min sync for 2027-05-04 and share an invite.

Marissa
